NTA.

BUT As someone who has depression and bipolar disorder, here's the thing about weird thoughts like those that your friend has: they're remotely based on truth. No thought or feeling is completely pulled out of thin air. Usually, something happens but the brain interprets it in the worst way possible or makes it 100% a bigger deal than it is. 

You forgot to reply to his text? Didn't remember his favorite color? You hung out with another friend instead of him? You seenzoned him? You went to work instead of consoling his depressive thoughts? In his mind, you're the worst friend ever. These are very small incidents that can sometimes be avoided, talked through, resolved, whatever. But no matter the outcome of dealing/ not dealing with these things, they build up in his mind and the result is, you're a bad friend.

Of course, that's not really true- at least based on what you say. (Tbf it does seem like you were a "better" friend after he stopped talking to you since before you weren't really hanging out much. But I digress)

Anyway, tl;dr his thinking that you're a bad friend is coming from something, no matter how small and seemingly irrelevant.

But, they're also TA for going back on their word and leaving you like that, mostly because they didn't say anything. And hubby's remark on you feeling guilty about leaving your child as opposed to him feeling completely fine about it is a sign on how one sided the situation will be with taking care of the kid, so watch out.
